newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ economists' inflation expectations rise - survey.
newsitem.headline: NZ economists' inflation expectations rise - survey.

text.p: New Zealand economists expect inflation in one, four and seven years' time to be higher than they did last October, while their growth outlooks are largely unchanged, according to a survey published on Friday.
The survey by the Alexander Consulting Group was based on responses from 16 organisations including banks, sharebrokers, fund managers and economic researchers.
It was the group's first since a centre-right coalition agreement last month, which widened the central Reserve Bank's target range for underlying inflation to 0-3 percent from 0-2 percent.

CPI inflation was expected to be 1.23 percent in a year's time, up from 1.14 percent in the October survey, while GDP growth in a year's time is picked at 2.72 percent versus 2.77 percent in the last survey.
Latest figures show the CPI rose 2.6 percent in the year to December and production-based GDP grew 2.3 percent in the year to September 1996.

Note: asterisked lines of figures are the result of the Alexander Consulting Group's October 1996 survey.
